title: Manyhands JSON v1 operation abandon preview
description: The data of a prepare envelope that gives a preview of operation abandon: the pending operation that will be closed, what it has left, and the confirmation an execute of the same command, repository and operation presents to close it. The operation is a pending local one, or a pending synchronization of the remote journal that no process of this host works under: one that is not bound to a promotion, a closure, a retirement or a local synchronization, has recorded no authority, owes no index hand-off and holds no integration or resolution work of its own. Its abandon is a hand-over: a person confirms it, having seen evidence. A prepare that gives no preview carries no preview data: a rejection, as for an operation ID no journal holds (operation_not_found), or one that is a key operation's or a remote operation's that is no such synchronization (invalid_input), busy for a synchronization another process of this host still works under, whose data blocked.schema.json describes, naming that operation, with operation.show offered for it, and a no-op for an operation that has ended. For a local operation the preview does not say whether a call is still working under it: the execute finds that out, and is busy when one is. For a synchronization the execute asks again, and is busy, naming the holder in data.blocker, when one works under it again.

confirmation_id.description: What an execute presents as its consent. It is accepted by one request.

expires_at.description: When the confirmation stops being accepted by a new request: ten minutes after the preview. A request that has accepted it is honored afterwards.

command.description: The command the confirmation is for, as an envelope names it.

effects.description: What the command will do, in the order it does it.

details.description: The operation that will be closed. Generic abandonment closes the local row and releases its unfinished request. Retirement instead retains that request identity, fences deletion, preserves remaining resources and settles local discovery before atomically recording abandonment. A synchronization ends cancelled, its push recorded refused when nothing answered it (the effect push_marked_rejected), and releases its unfinished request; it touches no file, nothing Git holds and no remote. The confirmation binds state and step, plus retirement epochs, removal flags and retained resources when retirement is not null, and for a synchronization its checkpoint, owner epoch and evidence; a changed snapshot is external_change.

retirement.description: Null for generic abandonment. A retirement retains its controlling request and every remaining resource; only its local discovery obligation is settled.

worktree_retained.description: Present or not safely known absent. This is conservative consent metadata, never cleanup authority.

branch_retained.description: Present or not safely known absent, including unreadable or redirected ref storage. Never cleanup authority.

root.description: The repository's root, as the operation's journal names it.

operation_id.description: The operation that will be closed.

action.description: What the operation does, as operation show names it. Null for an action this version does not know.

state.description: The state the operation is in, as operation show gives it.

step.description: The last step the operation recorded as done. Null when it recorded none.

item_id.description: The item the operation writes. Null for an operation that writes no item.

worktree.description: The worktree the operation writes in, relative to the repository's root with forward slashes: an item's own, or . for the primary worktree. Null for an operation that writes no file of a worktree, a synchronization among them, and for an item whose worktree is not there.

paths.description: The paths of the operation's target that differ from the head of their branch, uncommitted and untracked alike, relative to the repository's root with forward slashes: for an operation that writes an item, every such path of the item's worktree; for one that writes the configuration file, that file when it differs; none for a synchronization. The command leaves every one of them exactly as it is, for its user to commit or restore with Git. No content is given.

paths_complete.description: Whether paths is all of them. False when there are more than are listed, or the worktree could not be read: git status in the worktree then says what is there.

committed.description: Whether the operation recorded that it passed the point where its work is committed: for a save, its checkpoint; for an enablement, its initialization commit. False for a synchronization, which commits nothing of its own: what it moved is in evidence. The command leaves that commit where it is: abandoning undoes nothing.

request_id.description: The unfinished request that began the operation. Generic abandonment releases its record so its ID is free. When retirement is not null, its identity and operation mapping are retained permanently instead. Null when no such request is recorded.

files_changed.description: Whether the command changes or removes any file under the root. It never does: this is false.

git_state_changed.description: Whether the command changes anything Git holds: a commit, a branch, a worktree, the index or the configuration. It never does: this is false.

evidence.description: Null for a local operation. For a synchronization, what the person decides with: what its row last saw of the remote, the local branch now and the push it intended. Nothing is fetched and no remote is contacted for it. A push at push_prepared with the branch absent may still have reached the remote: the row says what it saw before the push. A push that returned (the state push_returned, or a publication attempt that returned) was taken by the remote after the row's last look, so nothing is said of the remote branch for it.

remote_ref_present.description: Whether the remote branch the operation publishes to was there when the row last looked: at the push endpoint for an operation that recorded a push (its newest publication attempt's look, once there is one past open), else at its fetch. Null for a row that recorded no look, and for one whose push returned after its last look.

local_oid.description: The commit the operation's local branch names now, read from Git. Null when the branch is not there.

remote_oid.description: The commit the remote branch named when the row last looked. Null when it was absent, or the row recorded no look.

push_oid.description: The commit the operation set out to push: its newest publication attempt's, else its push intent's. Null when it recorded no push.
